---
applyTo: "crates/thermo_physics/**,crates/thermo_runtime/**"
---

# Physics and world rules

Invariants for code in `thermo_physics` and `thermo_runtime`. Procedures (tests, baselines, fixtures) are in the `physics-change`, `save-format` and `headless-contract` skills.

- Index contract: cells and Verlet lists store indices into the primary `Vec<Ball2D>`. After any index-affecting mutation (`Vec::retain()`, `remove()`, `swap_remove()`), clear all neighbour lists and rebuild the cell grid immediately (`remove_invalid_balls`); never keep indices across a structural change. The one permutation that keeps the lists, the sort by cell (`reorder_balls_by_cell`), renumbers them with `Verlet::remap`; any new index-keyed per-ball state must be permuted there as well as cleared after `retain`.
- Force and potential match: `F = -dU/dr` everywhere, in the scalar path (`PairPotential::force` / `potential`) and the SIMD path (`force_simd` / `potential_simd`), for every `PairLaw` and in `CappedPotential`. A change to one needs the matching change to the others, an energy test, and verified energy conservation.
- Units: reduced Lennard-Jones units with Ar as the unit (`UnitSystem::REDUCED`, #405). Tests that assume reduced values of 1 use `SPECIES_AR`; test geometry set up in the former N₂ units is scaled (`N2_LENGTH`, `N2_SPEED` in the drift harness). A new built-in species is converted from Å, K and u with the Ar constants.
- Orientation (#348): a species with `inertia` has `θ`, `ω`, `α` on its balls (`Ball2D`, hot); the position update drifts `θ` (`advance_orientation`), the apply pass kicks `ω` from `ForceResult::torque` (`kick_rotation`) and adds `½ I ω²` to the kinetic energy. Every path that sums kinetic energy or temperature includes it (`LocalKineticStats` counts one degree of freedom per rotating ball); balls without inertia keep 0 and their arithmetic must stay bit-identical (guard with `inertia > 0`).
- MB water (#349): a species with `water` (`MbWater`) adds hydrogen bonds with water neighbours in the force pass (`SimulationEngine::add_hydrogen_bonds`, scalar, after the SIMD kernel): energy into `potential_energy` (counted by both balls), force, torque and virial. Its Lennard-Jones part goes through the pair table like any species. `MbWater::pair` must stay the exact derivative of its energy (`force_and_torque_match_finite_differences`). A species' `max_time_step` (water, H₂ #407, CO₂ #408) caps the step while it is present (`MainContent::active_time_step`); code that steps the world uses that, not the set `time_step()`.
- Rigid molecules (#406): a species with `molecule` (`LinearMolecule`, sites along the axis) has `ε = 0` and an envelope `σ`, so the pair table gives it a null pair (`PairLaw::is_null`, no cap); its interactions are the site–site pairs of `SiteTable` (`SimulationEngine::add_molecule_pairs`, scalar, only while a molecule species is present) and the soft walls act per site (`wall_forces`, with torque). Its box-wall contact is per end site (`Ball2D::execute_update_pos_molecule`, #408): a site within its contact distance that moves into a wall gets the rigid-body impulse at the site (translation and rotation, elastic), the overshoot is mirrored, and the walls book the momentum via `BounceInfo::wall_momentum`; line walls use the full half length. Config overrides (`[[potential.pair_override]]`, `[[walls.override]]`) that name a molecule species are rejected: they would not reach the sites. Keep `SiteTable::pair` the exact derivative of its energy (finite-difference test).
- Species (`ball_impl::species`): a ball stores a `SpeciesId`; mass, `σ`, `ε`, colour and `display_radius` come from the world's `SpeciesTable`, an `Arc` owned by `BallPhysics` (`SimulationWorld::species()` reads it there) and injected into the `BallFactory` (`BallFactory::with_species`, swapped only by `use_species`, which resets the species of new balls for another table) and every `RendererSnapshot`. `WorldFile::validate` and `SimConfig::validated_species` resolve it once as `ResolvedSpecies`, which `SimulationWorld::with_resolved` takes. Without a config `[[species]]` list it is the built-in library (`SpeciesTable::builtin()`: `N2`, the default species, the former size classes `XS`–`XL`, then `Ar` (the unit species, `σ = ε = m = 1`, #405), `Ne`, `CH4` (TraPPE-UA, #409), `O2`, `NH3`, `CH4_HCB` (the former `CH4`)); a list replaces the whole table and its first entry is the default. Never look species up in `SpeciesTable::builtin()` outside tests and the default; use the world's table. `display_radius` is for drawing only and must not reach the physics (`display_radius_does_not_change_physics`).
- Pair potentials (`ball_impl::pair_potential`): a `PairLaw` (e.g. `LennardJones { sigma, epsilon }`) is the bare law; `CappedPotential` adds the force cap and the cutoff shift once for every law; a `PairTable` holds one capped potential per species pair (Lorentz–Berthelot mixing: `σ_ij = (σ_i + σ_j)/2`, `ε_ij = √(ε_i ε_j)`, except pairs with a `PairOverride` from the config's `[[potential.pair_override]]`, kept by `BallPhysics::pair_overrides()`), and the `Potential` enum lists the laws in use. `CapSettings` (`max_force`, `core_stiffness`, `cutoff_factor`) is owned by the potential and fixed when it is built (read it via `BallPhysics::cap_settings()`); `PhysicsConstants` holds only runtime settings (gravity, a `UniformField`). Other external fields (`[[fields]]`, `ball_impl::external_field`, #347) implement `ExternalField` (`acceleration`, `potential`, with `acceleration = -∇U / m`), get a `Field` variant and are added in the kick (`fields_acceleration`), for new balls in `add_ball_and_register`, and to the potential energy by a pass in ball order; runs without fields must stay bit-identical. A new interaction law implements `PairLaw` (scalar, and `Lanes` for four pairs with different parameters), gets a `Potential` variant and a match arm in `simd_forces::force_simd`, which dispatches once per ball to the monomorphised `force_kernel`; the kernel gathers each chunk's four pair potentials by the neighbours' species (`CappedLanes::gather`), with no per-neighbour branching.
- Run settings (`application::sim_config`): the size of a new world (`[world] scale`, `WorldConfig::rect()`; a loaded save keeps its `world_rect`, a window resize keeps the world units per pixel), the time step, speed limit factor, force cap and cutoff (`CapSettings`), Verlet skin factor and snapshot interval come from `SimConfig` (defaults, then a `--config` TOML file, then CLI flags such as `--dt` and `--world-scale`); `MainContent::with_config` builds the world from it and `MainContent::config()` reads it back. A new tunable becomes a defaulted `SimConfig` key whose default is today's value, not a new constant. Saves store the config; changing a default changes how saves without a config run (see the `save-format` skill).
- Cutoff: all pair distances are centre distances. A pair interacts only for centre distance `< cutoff_ij` (`cutoff_factor * σ_ij`); its potential is shifted by `U(cutoff_ij)` (`pot_at_cutoff`) so it is zero there. Neighbour lists use the per-pair list radius `cutoff_ij + skin` (`BallPhysics::list_radius`) and may hold pairs beyond the cutoff; they must contribute no force or energy, otherwise every list change moves the total energy.
- Force capping: when centre distance `< r_cap` (per pair), the force is `max_force + core_stiffness * (r_cap - r)` with potential `U(r) = U(r_cap) - max_force * (r - r_cap) + 0.5 * core_stiffness * (r - r_cap)^2` (F = -dU/dr, repulsive). The slope keeps deeper overlaps pushing harder than shallow ones; do not flatten it: a flat cap lets crowded neighbours pin overlapping pairs (#240). `r_cap` is cached in each `CappedPotential` and computed by `force_cap_distance()` (Newton, accepted only if the root lies in `PairLaw::cap_search_range()` and hits `max_force`; otherwise a logged bisection over that range, by default `[0.1·σ, equilibrium distance]`); the law's `force_derivative` must be exact or Newton does not converge (#276).
- Wall contacts: box walls and line segments are resolved in the position update along the wall normal (`ball_impl::wall_contact`), not by projecting or mirroring the whole overshoot, which gains energy on every contact. A ball is reflected at the centre distance its `WallLaw` gives (`BallPhysics::wall_contact_distance`: `σ_i / 2` with hard walls, the backstop `backstop · σ_i` behind soft walls); wall code asks the law, it does not use a ball radius. The velocity update applies the returned `WallContact`s and books the momentum change as wall momentum.
- Soft walls (`[walls]`, default `model = "soft"`, #280): `SoftWalls` holds one `CappedPotential<LennardJones>` per species in the wall distance `z` (Lorentz–Berthelot with the wall pseudo-species, `[[walls.override]]`). `wall_forces::soft_wall_force` adds force and energy in the force pass: every box side by its signed distance, of each chain only the nearest line wall (nearest-feature rule, no energy bumps at joints; separate chains add up); balls flagged `leaving_wall` feel no line wall until they are past the cutoff (`wall_release_distance`). Its energy goes into `ForceResult::wall_potential` (not double counted), its force minus the ghost wall's into `wall_force`, booked as wall momentum `-F·dt`. Anything that sums the potential energy itself (tests, the drift harness) must add the wall energy. Placement keeps new balls at `BallPhysics::wall_placement_distance` (the potential minimum). Old saves migrate to `model = "hard"`; tests of the hard contact call `MainContent::use_hard_walls()`.
- Neighbour lists: a ball rebuilds its Verlet list when its displacement since its last rebuild exceeds skin/3 (`get_min_movement_for_update_hood`). Rebuilds are per ball and asynchronous, so skin/2 is not enough; the drift suite's stale-list check (`missed_neighbor_pairs`) guards this. Lists are sorted by ball index. The skin is `skin_factor · cutoff_factor · σ_N2` (`[neighbours]` in `SimConfig`).
- Cell grid: cells are at least the largest list radius among the species present in the world (`SimulationWorld::species_present`, `CellGrid::list_radius`; cell count rounded down). Adding a ball of a new species marks the need; `fit_cell_grid` rebuilds the grid before the next neighbour rebuild, when every ball is in its cell. The `cells` phase rebuilds the grid from all positions every step (`CellGrid::rebuild`); balls added in between go into its per-cell `late` lists. Never resize the grid between a position update and that rebuild.
- Overlap and placement checks use the edge gap of a pair, its centre distance minus its contact distance `σ_ij` (`BallPhysics::edge_gap` / `contact_distance`), which is zero where the pair potential crosses zero, also for an overridden pair. Without an override it equals the gap between contact discs (`σ/2` per ball, `Ball2D::get_edge_distance`). A `σ_ii` override also sets the species' wall contact (`σ_ii / 2`). Balls with NaN positions are invalid and must be removed.
- Reproducibility: results must not depend on the Rayon thread count or scheduling. Use `par_iter()` with read-only neighbour access, no shared mutable state in force loops, and no reductions whose order depends on work splitting; sums over balls run in a fixed order.
- SIMD kernels (`simd_forces`) use portable `std::simd` (`f32x4`) without runtime dispatch or multiversioning: the instruction set is fixed at compile time (target baseline in dev, `target-cpu=native` in the release and perf profiles). Compare f32 results and drift baselines only between builds for the same target and profile.
- Precision: a ball's position is f64 (`Ball2D::exact`); `get_position()` is its f32 copy. Move balls only through the setters (`set_position_and_update_tail`, the position update), never by writing the copy, and take differences of positions that feed forces from the f64 values (`KernelPoint` holds f32 offsets from f64 cell corners, `KernelFrame::point`; its difference is `Δcell · cell size + Δoffset`). Other f32 code loses resolution far from the origin (~3e-5 at 500): tests build worlds centred on the origin. Running totals and global statistics are f64 (#421): the simulation time, the step's energy, momentum and mass sums, the wall momentum, the thermostat chains and the temperature sums (`LocalKineticStats`); f32 stays in the per-ball and per-pair terms. A new accumulator follows the same rule.
